prompt:
You are shown a top-down map of a maze as a grid of characters, one character per cell.

- '#' is a wall (impassable).
- '.' is free floor.
- 'A' is the agent (a robot) standing on a free cell.
- 'G' is the goal, on a free cell.

Rows are printed top to bottom; the top row is the north edge of the map. Columns run west (left) to east (right). North = toward the top of the grid, south = toward the bottom, west = left, east = right.

Distances count cells. "Adjacent" means the 4 cells directly north, south, east and west of a cell (not the diagonals). The agent can move north, south, east or west through free cells ('.', 'A', 'G'), but never through walls ('#').

Map:
```
###############
#.............#
#.#####.###.###
#.......#...#.#
#.#####.#####.#
#...A.#.......#
###.###.#####.#
#.#.#...#...#.#
#.#.###.#.###.#
#.#...#.#.#...#
#.###.###G###.#
#.............#
###############
```

Questions about the map:
Q1. In which direction is the goal (G) from the agent (A)? (Answer with exactly one of: N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW)
Q2. How many of the 4 cells directly adjacent to the agent (north, south, east, west) are walls (#)? (Answer with a single digit 0-4)
Q3. Is the cell immediately west (left) of the agent a wall (#)? (Answer yes or no)
Q4. What is the Manhattan distance between the agent and the goal (counting steps north/south/east/west only, ignoring walls)? (Answer with a number)
Q5. Does any path exist from the agent to the goal moving only north/south/east/west through free cells (never through walls)? (Answer yes or no)
